question_text:
Convert the change in length data in Table to engineering stress and strain for the 1000-lb load. Give your answer as a tuple (Stress (psi), Strain (in./in.)).

Refer to Table:
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \multicolumn{4}{|l|}{TABLE 6-1 The results of a tensile test of a 0.505-in. diameter aluminum alloy test bar, initial length $\left(l_0\right)=2 \mathrm{in}$.} \\
\hline \multirow[b]{2}{*}{Load (lb)} & \multirow[b]{2}{*}{Change in Length (in.)} & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{Calculated} \\
\hline & & Stress (psi) & Strain (in./in.) \\
\hline 0 & 0.000 & 0 & 0 \\
\hline 1000 & 0.001 & 4,993 & 0.0005 \\
\hline 3000 & 0.003 & 14,978 & 0.0015 \\
\hline 5000 & 0.005 & 24,963 & 0.0025 \\
\hline 7000 & 0.007 & 34,948 & 0.0035 \\
\hline 7500 & 0.030 & 37,445 & 0.0150 \\
\hline 7900 & 0.080 & 39,442 & 0.0400 \\
\hline 8000 (maximum load) & 0.120 & 39,941 & 0.0600 \\
\hline 7950 & 0.160 & 39,691 & 0.0800 \\
\hline 7600 (fracture) & 0.205 & 37,944 & 0.1025 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}The units of each required answer are (psi, in./in), respectively.
response:
Stress = Load / Area, with area $A = \pi(d/2)^2 = \pi(0.2525)^2 \approx 0.2003\ \text{in}^2$, giving $\sigma = 1000/A \approx 4993$ psi. Strain = $\Delta l / l_0 = 0.001/2 = 0.0005$ in./in.

$$\boxed{(4993,\ 0.0005)}$$
